sections.section_title: The Question and the Torah's Answer
sections.summary: Paul poses the test case of Abraham and quotes Genesis 15:6 to establish that Abraham believed God and it was reckoned to him as righteousness, demonstrating that right standing before God was through faith, not works.

sections.section_title: The Logic of Wages versus Gift
sections.summary: Paul draws an analogy between wages earned and gifts freely given, establishing that justification is not a wage owed by God for works performed but a gift in which God reckons faith as righteousness, justifying the ungodly.

Paul cites Psalm 32 as David's confirmation that blessedness consists in having lawless deeds forgiven, sins covered, and sin not reckoned -- establishing the negative complement to Abraham's positive reckoning of righteousness apart from works.

Paul demonstrates from the Torah's own chronology that Abraham was reckoned righteous before circumcision, making him father of both uncircumcised believers and circumcised believers who walk in his pre-circumcision faith.

sections.section_title: The Promise, the Law, and Their Incompatibility
sections.summary: Paul argues that the promise to Abraham that he would be heir of the world came through the righteousness of faith, not through the law, since the law produces wrath by revealing transgression and would void the promise if it were the basis of inheritance.

sections.section_title: The Promise Rests on Grace, Abraham as Father of Many Nations
sections.summary: Paul states that the inheritance depends on faith so that it may rest on grace and be guaranteed to all Abraham's offspring, identifying Abraham as father of many nations before the God who gives life to the dead and calls into existence things that do not exist.

Paul describes Abraham's faith as trust in God's power despite impossible circumstances -- believing against hope, considering his dead body and Sarah's dead womb, yet being fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised.
Paul applies the reckoning of Genesis 15:6 to present believers who trust the God who raised Jesus, stating that Christ was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification.
